claims: The Renaissance was a 14th–17th century European cultural, artistic, and scientific rebirth following the Middle Ages.
The Renaissance was centered in Italy.
The Renaissance emphasized humanism, scientific inquiry, and artistic innovation.
Synonyms of Renaissance include rebirth, revival, renewal, awakening, and resurgence.
The Renaissance produced masterpieces by artists such as Leonardo da Vinci, Michelangelo, and Raphael.
Renaissance humanism shifted focus toward human potential and classical philosophy.
The Renaissance period witnessed innovations in optics, leading to the development of eyeglasses.
The Renaissance timeframe was roughly 14th–17th centuries.
The Renaissance involved art (painting, sculpture), architecture, literature, music, and science.
Key Renaissance artists include Michelangelo, Leonardo da Vinci, Botticelli, Donatello.
The Renaissance is divided into Early, High, and Late Renaissance (Mannerism).
The term "Renaissance" can also refer to modern companies or political movements, such as the French political party.
The term "Renaissance" can refer to organizations focusing on education, such as Renaissance Learning.
